I. Problem Statement Many job seekers find the application process tedious, frustrating, and time-consuming. This is because jobs are scattered across multiple platforms where each requiring lengthy and repetitive forms. This leaves the people seeking jobs feeling frustrated and often trying to look for other ways to apply for jobs. With 32.9 1 of South Africans unemployed as well as approximately 220 000 2 people graduating from South African universities every year, the demand for jobs continues to rise creating a growing need for a job application solution. This application will bring a new experience to the job application market making job applications easier than ever. With a modern and user friendly approach, the application will adopt a dating app style application. This means users will only have to swipe left and right on potential jobs and then rest will be handled by the application. The users will only have to input their information and CV once when they sign up and the app will do the rest of the administrative work automatically. This will also make a much better user experience for employers as all the job applications will be in one place where everything will be easy and simple to manage. This application will provide a simple and easy way for people to apply for jobs without long monotonous forms and spending long hours searching for job applications. The application will provide a high quality user experience that reduces time spent on applications and will solve the large problem that job seekers have today. II. User Stories and Prioritisation From the employee side of the application, the employee will sign up to the web application where they will be met with a few forms to fill out all their information needed as well as to attach a CV. Once this information is received, the user will be directed to the home page where it will get a view of a potential job which they meet the requirements for. This view will look the same as a dating website, only instead of people, the user will be viewing jobs. The user can then swipe left to decline the job or right to apply for the job. If the user swipes right, their application will be sent to the job where the job will have the choice of what the next step is (i.e. setting up a meeting, messaging the user or declining the job application. The user will also have a messaging page where they can respond to any messages sent to them by the employers. On the employers side of the application, the employers will sign up and fill out any necessary information needed. Once the information is received, they will be redirected to their home page which will show current job listings (if available, otherwise it will give them the option to make job listings) and the user will be able to click on any job listing and see if all the applicants. From there the user can either message or remove the applicant. III. Ensuring Client and End-User Satisfaction through Agile Development To ensure client and end-user satisfaction, the agile development methodology will be adopted. This allows for a collaborative approach with continuous feedback. Instead of the client receiving a product all at once, the product will be build over short development cycles where the client will be updated on whats going on and will be able to make small changes as the application is being developed. Meeting, progress updates and demos will be done on a regular basis to ensure the client is getting the product they want and are able to make any changes they would like as things are developed. This will ensure the client gets the product they wanted while also allowing the development team to stay on schedule to deliver the product when it has been planned to be finished. The target audience is mainly employers looking to hire new people as well as anyone unemployed and looking for a job. This application can also be used for people looking for freelance work however the main purpose of the application is for people looking for jobs. Will the job seeker have access to all the job applications and if so, how will they find the jobs that they are looking for? The application will use the requirements set up by the employers when they set up their job listings and only show those job listings to users who match those credentials. For example, if the job applications requires a matric certificate, only users who have a matric certificate will see the job listing on their feed. On top of that, the user will have more control over the jobs by having filters to see the job applications that they want to see such as jobs paying over a certain amount or jobs in a certain area. What information will the employer see when a user swipes right on their application? The employer will have certain options of what information they would like namely user details such as their name, age, qualifications, etc. as well as the users CV. The employee will be able to select what information they would like to receive when creating a job listing and will only receive the relevant information for that listing. What success metrics will be used? Businesses will be ranked on how many successful hires they have made. The more hires made, the more likely it is for the business to be at the top of the users feed. The less hires the business has made, the lower on the feed they will appear. This will promote businesses to constantly engage on the platform and look through new applications constantly. V. Unreasonable Requirements and Proposed Alternatives The app must guarantee job matches and hires for users No app will be able to guarantee this as it is almost impossible. Interviews, work culture fit and what the employer is looking for all play a role in if the job seeker is hired and thus, it is almost impossible to guarantee job matches. Alternatively, the application will optimize the user experience on both ends to ensure everything possible is done to get job seekers to be hired and job listings to be filled. Creating a video call service for meetings This would be an unreasonable requirement as this service is a large enough service to be an application by itself. The resources required would make the project exponentially larger and thus a much better alternative would to just use an existing platform such as Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, etc. and share the joining link through the messaging system the application will provide. The app will provide a CV builder This would be outside of the MVP (minimum viable product) and will take many resources as well as a lot of time to build. This would increase the project requirements as well as project resources drastically. Introduction This document describes the final group design for the Job Swipe app. This system aims to make the application and hiring process more straightforward with an intuitive swipe-based format. Job seekers can create profiles, upload resumes, and swipe right to apply - while employers promote listings and manage applicants from a central dashboard. Communication between users is handled by an encrypted role-based messaging system where employers initiate conversations and jobseekers can reply. The design tasks were assigned to group members in a way that each task covered all necessary elements. Each of the following sections within this document maps to an individual deliverables outlined in the project requirements UML class diagram, UML activity diagram, unit test tables, GUI models, and product and sprint backlogs. The design of all the artefacts has been performed at a low level to reduce ambiguity at the implementation and integration stages across different modules of the system. In particular, great attention has been given to the Networking, Security, and Communication Layer - as secure authentication, user data protection, and reliable real-time communications are of paramount importance. The design involves using JWT for auth, password hashing, encrypting sensitive information, in-app and email notifications. Performance, usability and maintainability as specified in the SRS have also been taken into account. The sections that follow aim to organise the description into layers of the system design for both functional aspects such as user registration, job listing, and messagingand non-functional requirements such as the security, scalability and the responsiveness of the app as a whole. The goal of these specifications are to establish a clear roadmap for the subsequent implementation phase and provides assurance that the final system will meet the specified requirements. II. Overview and Team Responsibilities JobSeekr is a web application that helps connect job seekers and employers. It follows a dating-app style format, which makes the user experience very simple. Job seekers simply swipe on the jobs they want to apply for, and the application will automatically be submitted for them. Employers can create one or multiple job listings and can view and manage all applications. JobSeekr streamlines the hiring process for both job seekers and employers, saving time while improving the overall experience of finding and filling jobs. Sean is responsible for system security, including user authentication, notifications, and data protection. I. Problem Statement Many job seekers find the application process tedious, frustrating, and time-consuming. This is because jobs are scattered across multiple platforms where each requiring lengthy and repetitive forms. This leaves the people seeking jobs feeling frustrated and often trying to look for other ways to apply for jobs. With 32.9 1 of South Africans unemployed as well as approximately 220 000 2 people graduating from South African universities every year, the demand for jobs continues to rise creating a growing need for a job application solution. This application will bring a new experience to the job application market making job applications easier than ever. With a modern and user friendly approach, the application will adopt a dating app style application. This means users will only have to swipe left and right on potential jobs and then rest will be handled by the application. The users will only have to input their information and CV once when they sign up and the app will do the rest of the administrative work automatically. This will also make a much better user experience for employers as all the job applications will be in one place where everything will be easy and simple to manage. This application will provide a simple and easy way for people to apply for jobs without long monotonous forms and spending long hours searching for job applications. The application will provide a high quality user experience that reduces time spent on applications and will solve the large problem that job seekers have today. II. User Stories and Prioritisation From the employee side of the application, the employee will sign up to the web application where they will be met with a few forms to fill out all their information needed as well as to attach a CV. Once this information is received, the user will be directed to the home page where it will get a view of a potential job which they meet the requirements for. This view will look the same as a dating website, only instead of people, the user will be viewing jobs. The user can then swipe left to decline the job or right to apply for the job. If the user swipes right, their application will be sent to the job where the job will have the choice of what the next step is (i.e. setting up a meeting, messaging the user or declining the job application. The user will also have a messaging page where they can respond to any messages sent to them by the employers. On the employers side of the application, the employers will sign up and fill out any necessary information needed. Once the information is received, they will be redirected to their home page which will show current job listings (if available, otherwise it will give them the option to make job listings) and the user will be able to click on any job listing and see if all the applicants. From there the user can either message or remove the applicant. III. Ensuring Client and End-User Satisfaction through Agile Development To ensure client and end-user satisfaction, the agile development methodology will be adopted. This allows for a collaborative approach with continuous feedback. Instead of the client receiving a product all at once, the product will be build over short development cycles where the client will be updated on whats going on and will be able to make small changes as the application is being developed. Meeting, progress updates and demos will be done on a regular basis to ensure the client is getting the product they want and are able to make any changes they would like as things are developed. This will ensure the client gets the product they wanted while also allowing the development team to stay on schedule to deliver the product when it has been planned to be finished. EPE 321  Project Proposal2025 University of PretoriaPage 1 of 3 IV. Follow-Up Questions to Clarify Client Requirements Who is this apps target audience? The target audience is mainly employers looking to hire new people as well as anyone unemployed and looking for a job. This application can also be used for people looking for freelance work however the main purpose of the application is for people looking for jobs. Will the job seeker have access to all the job applications and if so, how will they find the jobs that they are looking for? The application will use the requirements set up by the employers when they set up their job listings and only show those job listings to users who match those credentials. For example, if the job applications requires a matric certificate, only users who have a matric certificate will see the job listing on their feed. On top of that, the user will have more control over the jobs by having filters to see the job applications that they want to see such as jobs paying over a certain amount or jobs in a certain area. What information will the employer see when a user swipes right on their application? The employer will have certain options of what information they would like namely user details such as their name, age, qualifications, etc. as well as the users CV. The employee will be able to select what information they would like to receive when creating a job listing and will only receive the relevant information for that listing. What success metrics will be used? Businesses will be ranked on how many successful hires they have made. The more hires made, the more likely it is for the business to be at the top of the users feed. The less hires the business has made, the lower on the feed they will appear. This will promote businesses to constantly engage on the platform and look through new applications constantly. V. Unreasonable Requirements and Proposed Alternatives The app must guarantee job matches and hires for users No app will be able to guarantee this as it is almost impossible. Interviews, work culture fit and what the employer is looking for all play a role in if the job seeker is hired and thus, it is almost impossible to guarantee job matches. Alternatively, the application will optimize the user experience on both ends to ensure everything possible is done to get job seekers to be hired and job listings to be filled. Creating a video call service for meetings This would be an unreasonable requirement as this service is a large enough service to be an application by itself. The resources required would make the project exponentially larger and thus a much better alternative would to just use an existing platform such as Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, etc. and share the joining link through the messaging system the application will provide. The app will provide a CV builder This would be outside of the MVP (minimum viable product) and will take many resources as well as a lot of time to build. This would increase the project requirements as well as project resources drastically. Alternatively, users can use free or paid websites or applications such as Canva to build their CV and then upload their CV to this web app. EPE 321  Project Proposal2025 University of PretoriaPage 2 of 3 References 1 Statistics South Africa, Quarterly labour force survey (qlfs)  q1 2025, May 2025, accessed 2025-08-04. requirements.text: For Job Swipe Completed by   University of Pretoria Revision History Name Date Reason For Changes Version Daniel Kamener 11082025 Initial Version 1.0 Introduction Purpose The purpose of this web application is to provide a modern and simple for job seekers to apply for jobs as well as for employees to easily find applicants to hire. This application will use the same format as most dating apps where the job seeker can swipe left or right at potential jobs and if they swipe right, the application will apply to the job for them without them having to do tedious administrative work. The current version number is 1.0 as this is the concept for the application. This SRS covers the main features of the application but does not discuss the backend of the system, thus, only outlying the primary function of the system. Project Scope The scope of the application is for job seekers to browse potential jobs and apply for them by swiping right on the application, with the application automatically submitting their CV and personal details to potential employers. Employers will have a simple and easy to manage dashboard where they can look and manage applicants in one centralized application. This will save lots of time and frustration on both the employer and job seekers side. This aligns with broader business goals of using modern technology to make the hiring process easier, faster, and more accessible for both job seekers and employers through a simple and user-friendly mobile platform. References None Overall Description Product Perspective This product is a new, self-contained product to address the issues faced by job seekers and employers looking to hire. The concept came from trying to improve the old tedious methods of applying for jobs. This product is a standalone product, however, in the bigger picture it could integrate into HR platforms, applicant tracking systems, or job listing APIs. Block Diagram Product Functions For Job Seekers - Create personal profile and store CV - Browse available jobs using a swipe interface - Automatically submit a CV and user details to the employer if the user swipes right - View and manage history of jobs applied - Message the employer (Only allowed if the employer starts the chat) - Update profile For Employers - Make and manage job listings - View applicants in a centralized interface - View applicants CV and details - Message applicants - Update companyjob listing information System Functions - Create, remove and update users - Secure user authentication and data storage - Real time syncing between frontend and backend - Administration panel for monitoring app performance and user activity User Classes and Characteristics Job Seeker (Primary User Class) Frequency of use Very frequent as most users are anticipated to be job seekers Functions Used - Create personal profile and store CV - Browse available jobs using a swipe interface - Automatically submit a CV and user details to the employer if the user swipes right - View and manage history of jobs applied - Message the employer (Only allowed if the employer starts the chat) - Update profile Technical Expertise Basic to intermediate Privilege level Standard user  can only access user functions. Cannot access nor modify admin or employee functions EducationExperience Varies widely Pertinent Characteristics Job seekers require quick access to a simple and easy to use interface with minimal data entry. Employer (Secondary User Class) Frequency of use Depends on hiring needs Functions Used - Make and manage job listings - View applicants in a centralized interface - View applicants CV and details - Message applicants - Update companyjob listing information Technical Expertise Intermediate Privilege level Standard user  can only access user functions. Cannot access nor modify job seeker or employee functions EducationExperience Usually, professionals such as someone working in human resources Pertinent Characteristics Employers require an organized and easy to use interface to sort through all the applicant. Admin (Support Class) Frequency of use Occasional  used for maintenance and resolving any issues Functions Used - Create, remove and update users - Secure user authentication and data storage - Real time syncing between frontend and backend - Administration panel for monitoring app performance and user activity Technical Expertise Advanced Privilege level Has full access to the system EducationExperience Highly technical Pertinent Characteristics Admin focuses on reliability and ensures the system is working as expected. Also ensures the app is secure for all users Operating Environment This application will run on web browsers as it is a web application meaning it will be able to run on any hardware or operating system that can run a web browser. Design and Implementation Constraints The application must be a full stack application where the frontend must be implemented using HTML, CSS, JavaScript with React.js or Vue.js. The backend must be implemented with Node.js and Express or C or Python with DjangoFlask. The database must be PostgreSQL or MongoDB, and authentication must be handled using JSON Web Tokens. The performance requirements are that pages load in under two seconds on standard broadband, accessibility must comply with WCAG 2.1 AA standards and security must protect against XSS, CSRF, and SQL injection. Logging and error handling must include both client-side and server-side. Jira will be used for project management, Git for version control with regular commits, and Agile methodology with 12 week sprints. Assumptions and Dependencies All users are assumed to have the hardware to run a web browser as well as an internet connection. It is assumed users are willing to provide their personal details and CV upon registration and that employers will actively be using the application to look through job applications. All backend services such as hosting and backend operations will be hosted on a third-party cloud computing to ensure reliability and real-time syncing. External Interface Requirements User Interfaces The user interface for the application will be a minimalist and simple UI. For job seekers there will be a main card in the middle showing the job with arrows on the left and right to indicate to the user that they must either swipe left or right. On the top right will be a menu button where they can go onto their messages and settings. A mockup of what this will look like is shown below From the employer side, there will be multiple cards showing all their listings. When they click on one, it will take them to a page where all the applicants will be displayed. They will also have a menu button on the top right to be able to go to messages or settings. A mockup is displayed below Hardware Interfaces This application is designed for desktops, laptops and smartphones that have access to the internet and a web browser. Users will interact with the web application either by touch screen (for mobile phones) or with a keyboard and mouse (for laptops and desktops). The application will only collect location data from the user but no other hardware data. It communicated with backend servers with HTTPS. The Web application will interact with the devices network card to use the internet to send and receive data. Software Interfaces This application runs on a web browser which runs on the devices operating system. The application will be made with HTML, CSS, JavaScript and React for the frontend. For the backend, Node.js and express will be used and data will be stored using MongoDB. JSON web tokens will be used for web tokens and Jest will be used for testing. Documentation will be made with Markdown and OpenAI and the project will be managed through Jira. Finally, the application will be deployed with Netlify. Communications Interfaces This application communicates with backend servers through HTTPS which ensures secure and encrypted data transmission. All communication will be done through a RESTful JSON API (Application Protocol Interface). Web tokens will be used to ensure security by proving authentication. Data will be stored through a centralized database and will thus allow for synchronization. System Features Job Feed Description and Priority Job seekers will be given a feed of potential jobs where they will have the option to swipe left or right on the post. If they swipe left, the opportunity to apply for that position will be declined. If they, however, swipe right the application will automatically submit an application for the user to the application they swiped right to. This is a high priority feature as it is part of the core functionality of the application. StimulusResponse Sequences Functional Requirements JREQ-1 System will show user jobs retrieved from a database when the user loads the home page. JREQ-2 Each job will show the name, address, description and other optional information like amount they will pay, etc... JREQ-3 Users can swipe left to decline the offer JREQ-4 If the user swipes left, the offer will never show again and a new offer will show. JREQ-5 Users can swipe right to apply for the job JREQ-6 If the user swipes right, the system will apply for that position by sending the employer all the information needed. JREQ-7 Once the users information is sent, a new job listing will appear. JREQ-8 If no more jobs are available then a message will appear on the users feed. JREQ-9 The system will only apply once for a user to avoid duplicate applications Formal Use Cases Job Listing Description and Priority Employers are able to list jobs that they want applicants for to hire. They are able to create, delete and update details of each listing. They are also able to view all applicants that have applied for that position and either decline their application or message the applicant to set up a meeting or arrange the next step. This is a high priority feature as it is part of the core functionality of the application. StimulusResponse Sequences Functional Requirements EREQ-1 System will show user all current job listings EREQ-2 User is able to delete a job listing EREQ-3 User can update job listing information EREQ-4 User can view all applicants for a job listing EREQ-5 User can decline applicant EREQ-6 User can message applicant EREQ-7 User can create a job listing Formal Use Cases Other Nonfunctional Requirements Performance Requirements The page loads must be 2 seconds on standard broadband Security Requirements All users data including name, password, CV and any other data must be stored in a secure manner that cannot be accessed by anyone other than that user. Passwords must be encrypted using the latest standard of encryption AES-256 and data must be sent over a secure channel using HTTPS. Role based access will be made so that users will only be able to access what is relevant to them. The application must protect against XSS, CSRF, and SQL injections. Software Quality Attributes This application prioritizes usability. Users should be able to access and use this web application with minimal training. The application should be simple and easy to use. The application must also prioritize availability as the application must be up and running majority of the time and must follow WCAG 2.1 AA standards for UI. The application must also be maintainable with clean, commented and modular code that allows for bug fixes and future updates. Finally, the code must be scalable and must use modular code and data structures to allow extension of the program. Introduction This document describes the final group design for the Job Swipe app. This system aims to make the application and hiring process more straightforward with an intuitive swipe-based format. Job seekers can create profiles, upload resumes, and swipe right to apply - while employers promote listings and manage applicants from a central dashboard. Communication between users is handled by an encrypted role-based messaging system where employers initiate conversations and jobseekers can reply. The design tasks were assigned to group members in a way that each task covered all necessary elements. Each of the following sections within this document maps to an individual deliverables outlined in the project requirements UML class diagram, UML activity diagram, unit test tables, GUI models, and product and sprint backlogs. The design of all the artefacts has been performed at a low level to reduce ambiguity at the implementation and integration stages across different modules of the system. In particular, great attention has been given to the Networking, Security, and Communication Layer - as secure authentication, user data protection, and reliable real-time communications are of paramount importance. The design involves using JWT for auth, password hashing, encrypting sensitive information, in-app and email notifications. Performance, usability and maintainability as specified in the SRS have also been taken into account. The sections that follow aim to organise the description into layers of the system design for both functional aspects such as user registration, job listing, and messagingand non-functional requirements such as the security, scalability and the responsiveness of the app as a whole. The goal of these specifications are to establish a clear roadmap for the subsequent implementation phase and provides assurance that the final system will meet the specified requirements. II. Overview and Team Responsibilities JobSeekr is a web application that helps connect job seekers and employers. It follows a dating-app style format, which makes the user experience very simple. Job seekers simply swipe on the jobs they want to apply for, and the application will automatically be submitted for them. Employers can create one or multiple job listings and can view and manage all applications. JobSeekr streamlines the hiring process for both job seekers and employers, saving time while improving the overall experience of finding and filling jobs. To guarantee the projects success, each group member was given specific tasks to complete. Daniel was given the role of team leader and will focus on front-end design, making the screens and user interface that recruiters and candidates utilize. Nicole is in charge of the back-end job application procedure, which involves avoiding duplicate application creation and adding resumes and profiles. Jarryd is in charge of back end and manages the job listings for recruiters, providing functionality to add, edit, and remove job posts. Somto creates and manages the database and server, constructs the API, and makes sure that data is efficiently and safely stored. Tshego handles the AI aspect of the system and works on the Help Bot, which answers user questions and guides applicants through the system. Sean is responsible for system security, including user authentication, notifications, and data protection. Together, these roles make sure the systems front-end, back-end, database, security, and support are all built and work well together EPE 321  Design Document  Group 11 2025 University of PretoriaPage 1 of 24 III.
